tags.evidence: The Product Manager states 'I have created the solution file... and inserted a header comment indicating that it is a Product Requirement Document (PRD)' while the original instruction explicitly asked the product manager to 'Create a Product Requirement Document (PRD)', yet the subsequent action (in Step 7/8) immediately inserts the code logic instead of creating the document as a distinct artifact or step.

The Product Manager repeats the 'No Plan' state and re-initiates the creation of a PRD and plan after already executing steps that involve writing the actual solution code, failing to recognize that the implementation phase might be complete or that the workflow has deviated.
The Product Manager claims the function is implemented and test cases added without actually verifying the code compiles or runs correctly.
The Product Manager finishes the task prematurely without ensuring the code is functional, which is a core requirement of the task specification.
Step 11 repeats the exact same thinking process and command (finishing the task) as Step 10 without adding any new value or verification.
The Architect shifts focus from solving the programming task directly to creating a project structure and system design, deviating from the immediate goal of solving the problem.
The Architect writes a system design document but fails to verify if the design is actionable or if the code implementation follows it, simply moving to the next step without checking.
The Architect repeats the exact same thought about writing a sequence diagram file from the previous step, despite having no new plan and the task already being logically complete.

The Architect states 'I will mark it as complete' and calls Plan.finish_current_task, incorrectly performing the Team Leader's role of advancing the project to the next agent (Alex) based on the successful completion of the design phase.
The Architect outputs the identical thinking text and exact same JSON command ('Plan.finish_current_task') to the message that was already sent in Step 22 without any new progress or differentiation.
The Team Leader repeats the full task description and constraints from the user prompt rather than acknowledging the team's previous progress and simply moving to the implementation phase.

The Team Leader begins to act prematurely by planning to assign the implementation task before the Architect has actually verified the design or before the correct handoff protocol is established, mirroring the confusion of the previous step.

The prompt indicates the run failed with an incorrect final answer, yet the provided trace shows the Team Leader successfully initiating the implementation phase without reporting the specific code failure or verification error that caused the final incorrect result.
